title: When part of the test can only run on Matt's machine, how do those results get into the report?
lead: Should the expedition finish as usual and, when you paste back the results from your machine, a short follow-up job update the report and its pull request? I recommend that: the expedition never waits on you, and the report still ends up with the real-hardware numbers.
for_you: The report lists what to run yourself (often one small local page) with a results block to copy
Paste the block into the thread or use 'Paste results' on the finished card; a few minutes later the PR carries the real result
The follow-up has its own small budget, separate from the expedition's
context: Spec section 12, question 3 (memo M044). The reference run's GPU test needed Matt's RTX card: within one float step of the CPU, with 85% of the pipeline time on the CPU side, found only on real hardware. Scoping and the advisor checkpoint (2026-11-16) agree on B, built after phase 5.

options.name: Report only
options.summary: The report lists what to run; what you do with the result is up to you.
cons: The report stays wrong on exactly the items it couldn't run

options.name: Short follow-up job after you paste
options.summary: One small verifier job reads your pasted results and the report, updates the build status and how-it-ran sections, and pushes to the same draft PR.
pros: The expedition never waits; the report ends up right
cons: One more small piece to build, after phase 5

options.name: Keep the expedition open until you paste
options.summary: The Lead stays alive and the run waits for your results.
cons: Breaks the time and budget envelope; holds a Lead for hours or days

recommendation: B: the report gets the real numbers without holding the expedition open.
change_mind: If you rarely paste results back, A is enough.
